forcedChoices.choice: el serafín ... su pupilo mortal (masculine noun)
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish 'serafín' is masculine; the English 'her' cannot carry over without an ungrammatical agreement, so the possessive 'su' keeps it neutral.

forcedChoices.choice: tú (tu buen espíritu, de ti, contigo)
forcedChoices.reason: English 'you' in the psalm is singular or plural; 'your name' and 'this Divine Presence' support one addressee.
Spanish forces a gender; feminine matches 'sabiduría' and 'filosofía', the nouns it is compared with.
Spanish 'agresivo' reads as hostile; 'emprendedor' keeps the sense of outgoing initiative.
English 'yourself' is singular, but the passage addresses the readers, and the Spanish rules ask for 'ustedes'.
Two English words need two Spanish words so the sentences keep their distinction.
